post.caption: This garnet has more fire than diamond. Demantoid is the green variety of andradite garnet, and the name comes from an old German word for diamond. Its fire, called dispersion, measures 0.057, against 0.044 for diamond. Chromium makes it green, and iron can push it toward yellow. Fine fibers that fan out inside are called horsetail inclusions, and collectors prize them as typical of stones from Russia. In Russia's Ural Mountains, it was first mistaken for peridot. Peter Carl Fabergé made jewelry with demantoid garnets. At 6.5 to 7 on the Mohs scale, rings need protective settings.
